evidence:
Row 19 (workbook Quality Checks C20/D20: 'solve.sh installs to the expected paths and the reference runs under the stated contract. (Network is public - fetching or installing at start is not a defect.)'. Internal Quality Checks C20 has the older no-network wording and no annotation columns E-G for this row. The Quality Checks wording and the SKILL.md delivery profile (network public) govern.) Skill references/quality-checks.md s.19 asks for: valid bash, a shebang, LF line endings, the app written to /app and nothing to /tests, /logs/verifier or /solution, a start as node /app/server.js, DB_PATH honoured, idempotent seeding, and no pkill or NODE_ENV=production.

STATIC (frozen task .qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r4/task):
- solution/solve.sh has 36 lines: line 1 '#!/bin/bash', line 2 'set -euo pipefail', and 0 CR bytes. It writes only to /app: 'mkdir -p /app', then 'cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/' (the same install idiom as the template solve.sh), then 'rm -f -- "$database_path" "$database_path-wal" "$database_path-shm"'. Here database_path is realpath -m of ${DB_PATH:-/app/app.db}, and the script refuses it unless it is under /app/*. The embedded node /proc scan runs only when a database file already exists, so a fresh install exits 0 immediately. There is no pkill, no NODE_ENV, no write to /tests, /logs/verifier or /solution, no network install and no nproc.
- The installed tree is 11 files: package.json, server.js, src/{bootstrap,db,index}.js, src/seed_data.json, public/{index.html,styles.css,js/app.js,js/board.js,js/threads.js}. No node_modules and no *.db file are shipped.
- Entry: server.js calls require('./src/index.js'). In the main thread, index.js runs bootstrap.start(). Its http server listens on Number(process.env.PORT||3000) on 0.0.0.0 and answers GET/HEAD /api/health (and /health) without touching the DB. The Express/SQLite app runs in a worker_thread of the same process on 127.0.0.1 at an ephemeral port, and the main server proxies to it. This matches instruction.md ('start with node /app/server.js, listen on port 3000 (honour PORT), expose GET /api/health as a check that never touches the database, serve the UI as well as the API from that one process') and integration.md ('GET /api/health answers before database work can block startup').
- DB: src/db.js:9 'const DB_PATH = process.env.DB_PATH || path.join(__dirname, '..', 'app.db');' gives /app/app.db by default and honours DB_PATH. The WAL files sit beside the DB, so writes stay under /app or DB_PATH as integration.md requires.
- Seed: src/db.js:10 reads path.join(__dirname,'seed_data.json'). src/seed_data.json is byte-identical (cmp) to environment/assets/seed_data.json, so the app does not depend on /assets at runtime ('/assets and /instructions are unavailable at runtime'). seedIfEmpty seeds only when the users table is empty, so seeding is idempotent and a restart never reseeds.
- Paths are __dirname-relative (index.js:42 PUBLIC_DIR). This holds up under the different-cwd, locked-down launch that integration.md describes and test.sh performs ('setsid env -i ... setpriv --reuid=65534 node /app/server.js' with DB_PATH=/app/app.db and HOME=/tmp/submission).
- Dependencies: only express, better-sqlite3 and node built-ins. package.json pins express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1, the same versions installed globally in both environment/Dockerfile and tests/Dockerfile (both use the node:22-bookworm-slim runtime). They resolve through NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules, which test.sh passes. There is no run-time install. index.html loads only same-origin /styles.css and /js/*.js.
- tests/test.sh and tests/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff).

RUNTIME (raw-evidence-index.json): I re-hashed all 8 artifacts and all match. All 12 matching_source_files hashes match the frozen solution bytes, including solve.sh 1df2ed04....
- qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/via-solve.sh installs with the task's own solve.sh into an empty /app, chowns /app to 65534, and runs the driver as uid 65534 with only NODE_PATH set.
- results/via-solve.log reports 'solve.sh installed: 11 files', then 26 PASS groups. These include 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages, unread counts and activity without reseeding; live updates resume' and 'no JavaScript page errors'.
- workspace.cjs:16 launches spawn('node',['/app/server.js'],{cwd:'/tmp', env:{PATH,HOME:'/tmp',NODE_PATH,PORT:'3000',DB_PATH:'/tmp/hireops-workspace.db'}}). Line 552 restarts it (SIGTERM, then relaunch). The run therefore shows a different cwd, a cleared environment, DB_PATH honoured outside /app at runtime, uid 65534 and data surviving a restart.

LESSONS (handoffs/LESSONS_FROM_COLDERWATER_2026-10-08.md) that bear on row 19: lesson 19 asks for a scripted golden harness that installs with solve.sh, launches like test.sh and does a real restart. via-solve.sh and workspace.cjs do this in substance, with small differences from test.sh. The driver does not use setsid/env -i exactly, nor the generated app-restart.sh process-group kill, and its DB_PATH is /tmp rather than /app/app.db. The run used image tag hireops-verifier:20261002-permission-repair, and the index does not tie its build to the frozen tests/Dockerfile (which is template-identical). solve.sh ran in the verifier image, not the agent image; both use node:22-bookworm-slim node and the coreutils realpath. Lessons 15 and 16 (strength of the restart check, double grading) are criterion-design rows, not this row. Lesson 13 does not apply because the reference uses no external address.

ADVERSARIAL: (a) A broken reference could pass this row by reading /assets/seed_data.json at runtime or writing the DB relative to the cwd. Both are ruled out: the seed is read via __dirname, the DB path is __dirname-based or DB_PATH, and the run from cwd /tmp passed. (b) A conforming setup could fail because solve.sh exits 1 if DB_PATH points outside /app at install time. Harbor's oracle solve phase does not set DB_PATH, and test.sh sets it only for the launched app, so this cannot fail the oracle. solve.sh also deliberately refuses a re-install while a server holds the DB, but a fresh oracle /app has no DB. No defect found.

GAPS (not waived; this row can be decided without them): the evidence index holds no full configured verifier run of test.sh against the solve.sh-installed golden ('Full configured grading/workload ... Oracle/target scores are absent'). The exact test.sh launch path is therefore covered only by equivalence. That evidence belongs to the separate runtime records. No Oracle or portal score is claimed.
